output_text:
Repo: https://github.com/clawdbot  
GitHub issues/comments/PR comments: use literal multiline strings or `-F - <<'EOF'` (or $'...') for real newlines; never embed "\\n".  

Source code: `src/` (CLI wiring in `src/cli`, commands in `src/commands`, web provider in `src/provider-web.ts`, infra in `src/infra`, media pipeline in `src/media`).  
Tests: colocated `*.test.ts`.  
Docs: `docs/` (images, queue, Pi config). Built output: `dist/`.  
Plugins/extensions: `extensions/*` (workspace packages). Keep plugin-only deps in the extension `package.json`; do not add them to the root `package.json` unless core uses them.  

Installers served from `https://clawd.bot/*`: live in sibling repo `../clawd.bot` (`public/install.sh`, `public/install-cli.sh`, `public/install.ps1`).  

Messaging channels: always consider **all** built-in + extension channels when refactoring shared logic (routing, allowlists, pairing, command gating, onboarding, docs).  
Core channel docs: `docs/channels/`  
Core channel code: `src/telegram`, `src/discord`, `src/slack`, `src/signal`, `src/imessage`, `src/web` (WhatsApp web), `src/channels`, `src/routing`  
Extensions (channel plugins): `extensions/*` (e.g. `extensions/msteams`, `extensions/matrix`, `extensions/zalo`, `extensions/zalouser`, `extensions/voice-call`)  

Docs hosted on Mintlify (docs.clawd.bot).  
Internal doc links: root-relative, no `.md`/`.mdx` (example: `[Config](/configuration)`).  
Section cross-refs: anchors on root-relative paths (example: `[Hooks](/configuration#hooks)`).  
When Peter asks for links, reply with full `https://docs.clawd.bot/...` URLs (not root-relative).  
When you touch docs, end the reply with the `https://docs.clawd.bot/...` URLs you referenced.  
README (GitHub): keep absolute docs URLs (`https://docs.clawd.bot/...`) so links work on GitHub.  
Docs content must be generic: no personal device names/hostnames/paths; use placeholders like `user@gateway-host` and “gateway host”.  

Runtime baseline: Node **22+** (keep Node + Bun paths working).  
Install deps: `pnpm install` (also supported: `bun install` keep `pnpm-lock.yaml` + Bun patching in sync when touching deps/patches).  
Prefer Bun for TS execution: `bun <file.ts>` / `bunx <tool>`.  
Run CLI dev: `pnpm clawdbot ...` (bun) or `pnpm dev`.  
Node supported for `dist/*` runs + production installs.  

Type-check/build: `pnpm build` (tsc).  
Lint/format: `pnpm lint` (oxlint), `pnpm format` (oxfmt).  
Tests: `pnpm test` (vitest); coverage: `pnpm test:coverage`.  
Language: TS (ESM). Prefer strict typing; avoid `any`.  
Oxlint/Oxfmt formatting; run `pnpm lint` before commits.  
Brief comments for tricky logic.  
Keep files concise; extract helpers instead of “V2” copies; use existing patterns for CLI options + DI via `createDefaultDeps`.  
Aim keep files ~700 LOC; guideline only. Split/refactor when it improves clarity/testability.  

Naming: use **Clawdbot** for product/app/docs headings; use `clawdbot` for CLI command, package/binary, paths, config keys.  
stable: tagged releases only (e.g. `vYYYY.M.D`), npm dist-tag `latest`.  
beta: prerelease tags `vYYYY.M.D-beta.N`, npm dist-tag `beta` (may ship without macOS app).  
dev: moving head on `main` (no tag; `git checkout main`).  

Framework: Vitest w/ V8 coverage thresholds (70% lines/branches/functions/statements).  
Naming: match source names with `*.test.ts`; e2e in `*.e2e.test.ts`.  
Run `pnpm test` (or `pnpm test:coverage`) before pushing when touching logic.  
Live tests: `CLAWDBOT_LIVE_TEST=1 pnpm test:live` or `LIVE=1 pnpm test:live`.  
Docker live: `pnpm test:docker:live-models`, `pnpm test:docker:live-gateway`.  
Onboarding Docker E2E: `pnpm test:docker:onboard`.  
Full kit: `docs/testing.md`.  
Pure test additions/fixes generally no changelog unless user-facing or requested.  

Mobile: before simulator, check connected real iOS+Android devices and prefer them when available.  

Commits: `scripts/committer "<msg>" <file...>`; avoid manual `git add`/`git commit`.  
Commit messages: concise, action-oriented (e.g. `CLI: add verbose flag to send`).  
Group related changes; avoid unrelated refactors.  

Changelog: latest released version at top (no `Unreleased`); after publishing bump and start new top section.  
PRs: summarize scope, note testing, mention user-facing changes/new flags.  
PR review flow: if given PR link, review via `gh pr view`/`gh pr diff` and do **not** change branches.  
Review mode: read `gh pr view/diff`; **do not** switch branches; **do not** change code.  
PR review calls: prefer a single `gh pr view --json ...`; run `gh pr diff` only when needed.  
Before starting review when GH Issue/PR pasted: run `git pull`; if local changes/unpushed commits, stop+alert before reviewing.  

Landing mode: create integration branch from `main`, bring PR commits (**prefer rebase**; merge allowed when safer), apply fixes, add changelog (+ thanks + PR #), run full gate locally (`pnpm lint && pnpm build && pnpm test`), commit, merge back to `main`, then `git switch main` (never stay on topic branch). Contributor needs to be in git graph after landing.  

Multi-agent safety: do **not** create/apply/drop `git stash` entries unless explicitly requested (incl `git pull --rebase --autostash`). Assume other agents may be working; keep unrelated WIP untouched and avoid cross-cutting state changes.  
Multi-agent safety: when user says "push", may `git pull --rebase` to integrate latest changes (never discard other agents' work). When "commit", scope to your changes only. When "commit all", commit everything in grouped chunks.  
Multi-agent safety: do **not** create/remove/modify `git worktree` checkouts (or edit `.worktrees/*`) unless explicitly requested.  
Multi-agent safety: do **not** switch branches/check out a different branch unless explicitly requested.  
Multi-agent safety: running multiple agents is OK if each has its own session.  
Multi-agent safety: when you see unrecognized files, keep going; focus on your changes and commit only those.  

If you review a PR and later do work: land via merge/squash (no direct-main commits) and add PR author as co-contributor.  
When working on PR: add changelog entry w/ PR number + thank contributor.  
When working on issue: reference issue in changelog entry.  
When merging a PR: leave PR comment explaining exactly what we did + include SHA hashes.  
When merging PR from new contributor: add their avatar to README “Thanks to all clawtributors” thumbnail list.  
After merging: run `bun scripts/update-clawtributors.ts` if missing, then commit regenerated README.  
`sync`: if working tree dirty, commit all changes (sensible Conventional Commit), then `git pull --rebase`; if rebase conflicts and cannot resolve, stop; else `git push`.  

GitHub issue/PR tasks: When working on a GitHub Issue or PR, print the full URL at the end of the task.  

Web provider: creds at `~/.clawdbot/credentials/`; rerun `clawdbot login` if logged out.  
Pi sessions: `~/.clawdbot/sessions/` by default; base dir not configurable.  
Environment vars: see `~/.profile`.  

Never commit/publish real phone numbers, videos, or live configuration values. Use fake placeholders in docs/tests/examples.  

Release flow: always read `docs/reference/RELEASING.md` and `docs/platforms/mac/release.md` before any release work; do not ask routine que
